title: His Excellency the Spill
original_pitch: A court painter combs floating pigment into a ministerâ€™s majestic profile. A sneeze gives him three chins. The minister storms in. His reflection in the tray supplies a fourth. The printer takes an impression before anyone can object.
selection_justification: Surface marbling can turn portraiture into a fluid political joke, with a printed impression as an irreversible punchline.
adaptation: Floating pigment forms a grand ministerial profile in a gilded tray. A sneeze jolts the pigment into extra chins. The minister approaches as an ivory sheet lifts the fixed caricature.
story_beats: 4–7 s: sneeze distorts the floating profile
7–10 s: the offended minister leans over the tray
10–14 s: paper lifts the fixed caricature
music_prompt: Fourteen second instrumental court comedy. Harpsichord, bassoon, plucked strings. Exaggerated royal dignity, one sudden musical stumble at five seconds, mischievous descending bassoon at eight, final stamped chord at twelve. No singing, no speech.
sfx_prompt: An exaggerated single adult sneeze, a small liquid splash, then wet paper peeling slowly from a shallow printmaking tray. No words, no music.
